page: Vultr voc-s-16c-128gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs, derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. Memory capacity is provisioned at 128.0 GB, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. Local storage is bundled with the instance, consisting of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2912.97 and a Geekbench text processing score of 2587.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core and memory subsystem benchmarks generally align with the middle 50% average. The multi-core stress-ng CPU performance is recorded at 46204.81, while the Geekbench multi-core score reaches 14048.0. Memory bandwidth tests show an average performance profile, with uncached large-block read speeds at 123.94 GB/sec and write speeds at 70.41 GB/sec. Database operations under Passmark register at 7168.29, and Redis SET operations achieve 28.04 million operations per second.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is characterized by its high storage-to-vCPU and memory-to-vCPU ratios, offering a dense allocation of 128 GB RAM and nearly 4 TB of NVMe storage on a 16-vCPU footprint. A notable tradeoff is the 2.0 GHz clock speed, which limits raw single-threaded execution velocity compared to high-frequency compute-optimized instances, though its single-core stress-ng results remain strong. The instance is suited for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads, including relational databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and medium-scale web serving.
